definition: Hierarchical classification is a system of grouping things according to a hierarchy.
details: In the field of machine learning, hierarchical classification is sometimes referred to as instance space decomposition, which splits a complete multi-class problem into a set of smaller classification problems.

explainer.lead: Hierarchical classification groups things according to a hierarchy. In machine learning it is sometimes called instance space decomposition, splitting a complete multi-class problem into smaller classification problems.

tiers.eli5: Instead of picking one label from a giant flat list, you first pick a broad category, then a subcategory, then a sub-subcategory, like browsing folders.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers decompose a large multi-class problem into a set of smaller classifiers arranged in a hierarchy. A pitfall is error propagation: a mistake at a high level constrains every choice below it.
tiers.paperLevel: Hierarchical classification is a system of grouping things according to a hierarchy; in machine learning it is referred to as instance space decomposition, which splits a complete multi-class problem into a set of smaller classification problems.

explainer.example: A document classifier first predicts a top-level topic, then uses a separate model within that branch to pick the specific subtopic.
